reason: The printer supports an object member constructed as cJSON_Raw, but the old harness prints only parsed trees. Parsing never creates cJSON_Raw. This coverage gap is preexisting: the same tuple and blocker exist before and after g0002.
finite_witness: Supported setup: create an object, add raw member ("x", "1e0"), then print it unformatted to obtain {"x":1e0}. The old harness can accept input bytes 0000{"x":1e0}\0, but parsing makes the member a Number and printing emits {"x":1}; no input bytes make the harness construct the Raw member.

scope_contract.reason: Object printing passes member values to print_value, whose supported Raw case emits the stored text. The harness's printing operations take cJSON objects, so this supported object state is within their operational surface.

evidence.dependency_reason: Defines the supported raw value rendering.
Provides a supported way to insert a Raw object member.

feasible_trigger.reason: A one-level object with a Raw member holding "1e0" is a finite supported state. The harness's input format admits the corresponding JSON text, but its setup obtains the tree solely by parsing.

evidence.dependency_reason: Constructs and inserts the Raw member.
Constructs the object used in the supported setup.

observable_consequence.reason: Raw printing preserves "1e0". Parsing that text creates a Number with value 1, which the number printer emits as "1". Thus the supported raw member output is unreachable through the harness.

evidence.dependency_reason: Separates Number and Raw rendering and copies Raw text verbatim.
Parsing 1e0 stores numeric value 1 and Number type.
An integral numeric value is printed with its integer spelling.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete parser value dispatcher has no Raw case, object parsing delegates each member value to it, and the complete harness has no construction or insertion step. Its optional minification acts on a separate copy after printing, so it does not supply an equivalent route.

evidence.dependency_reason: Complete value dispatcher rules out creating Raw by parsing.
Object member values use that dispatcher.

identity_preserved.reason: Before and after g0002, the assessed behavior is printing a constructed Raw object member. Both object printers delegate the member value to print_value, and the unchanged harness still creates its printed tree only by parsing. The added depth guard does not block the one-level supported setup.

evidence.dependency_reason: The new guard applies only at the nesting limit.
Before parser has the same Raw-creation blocker.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: Print an object member whose cJSON_Raw valuestring is emitted verbatim, such as {"x":1e0}.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Create an object and insert a Raw member with cJSON_AddRawToObject(object, "x", "1e0").
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: Parse fuzz-supplied JSON into a tree, then print that parsed tree without modifying its members.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: Printing a constructed Raw object member; parsing {"x":1e0} instead creates a Number and prints {"x":1}.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: None in the complete old harness: its parser cannot create Raw, and minification occurs on a separate copy after printing.
